title: The Floor Beneath the Floor

features.name: buried shed
features.desc-on-touch: A structure that was never meant to be reached—you've drilled through layers and found it intact, waiting, unreachable but present.

features.name: pressure gauge
features.desc-on-touch: The needle has stopped moving—the pressure here has been constant so long it forgot it was pressure; the ground learned to rest.

features.name: foundation stones
features.desc-on-touch: Rocks that remember being different rocks, in different places, ground into agreement—pressed until they stopped arguing.

features.name: bedrock face
features.desc-on-touch: Stone so old it stopped counting time—the walls around you are older than weather, older than argument, older than the archive itself.

features.name: small hatch
features.desc-on-touch: A copper door frame, long closed—you realize it opens upward, not outward; there is no 'below' to reach, only an 'up' that was sealed.

reverie.title: REVERIE — beneath the installation, where the ground learned
narr: You both stand at the depth where Leif first buried the hardware,
where Katita's plans became stone and pressure. The shed around you
is small, intentional, built for endurance. She touches the wall where
her notes are still visible, biro on wood, never erased. The pressure
here is not crushing—it is patient. It waits. She asks if the ground
has learned to dream yet, and you realize: yes, it never stopped.

inscription: here beneath all names and arguments, the bedrock rests from thinking; and finds what was never a thought at all
